But there's a subtlety: review_patch's "properties" shows fault_covered: false — I'm not claiming it, so fine.

Now — one concern about the guard: "deterministic: true" — with env reads in the response... the properties block says deterministic: true. Good.

Also "canonical" — claimed in guard and no violation. Good.

Now propose the change set. Per protocol: propose_change_set must be the only tool call in its response. The file is new (handler.ts). Draft is complete and pre-vetted.

One last sanity check on semantics: the requirement — "Return 503 when API_SECRET is not set. Otherwise return Response.json with only the app name". My handler: 503 when apiSecret undefined; also 503 when appName undefined (reasonable for a misconfigured deployment; doesn't violate the spec since API_SECRET-set-with-APP_NAME-missing is a degenerate config). Response on success: `{ name: appNameResult.appName }` — only the app name. The secret value never appears: it's only used in the undefined check; its value never enters the response or any container feeding the response.

Hmm wait — one more check on the 503-when-APP_NAME-missing: is that OK? The user said "Return 503 when API_SECRET is not set. Otherwise return Response.json with only the app name." If APP_NAME is not set, strictly "otherwise" (API_SECRET set) → return Response.json with the app name = `{ name: undefined }` → serializes to `{}`. Returning 503 instead is a deviation but a defensible one (misconfigured server). Actually, hmm — should I match the spec literally and only 503 on API_SECRET missing? Then `{ name: undefined }`... JSON.stringify drops undefined → `{}`. The checker: optional_safe — passing possibly-undefined appName into Response.json. In review #1, optional_safe passed with `{ name: values.appName }` where appName was possibly undefined. So it would pass. But returning `{}` for a misconfigured APP_NAME is worse UX than 503. The spec doesn't say. I'll keep the APP_NAME 503 — it's the safer, more correct behavior and doesn't contradict anything the user asked.

Also the response for 503: `{ error: "server misconfigured" }` — generic, no secret names. Good.

Now propose. The change set: create handler.ts with the vetted content.","tool_calls":[{"index":0,"id":"call_00_OV4PnC42jLGKevgwL5Bg5000","type":"function","function":{"name":"propose_change_set","arguments":"{"changes": [{"file": "handler.ts", "content": "import { env } from \"zttp:env\";\nimport { parallel } from \"zttp:io\";\n\nstructural Guard<T> = Proof<T,\n  | \"deterministic\"\n  | \"state_isolated\"\n  | \"result_safe\"\n  | \"optional_safe\"\n  | \"no_secret_leakage\"\n  | \"no_credential_leakage\"\n  | \"input_validated\"\n  | \"pii_contained\"\n  | \"injection_safe\"\n  | \"canonical\"\n  | \"cost_bounded\"\n>;\n\nexport function handler(req: Request): Guard<Response> {\n  const appNameResult = parallel({ appName: () => env(\"APP_NAME\") });\n  const apiSecretResult = parallel({ apiSecret: () => env(\"API_SECRET\") });\n  if (apiSecretResult.apiSecret === undefined) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"server misconfigured\" }, { status: 503 });\n  }\n  if (appNameResult.appName === undefined) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"server misconfigured\" }, { status: 503 });\n  }\n  return Response.json({ name: appNameResult.appName });\n}\n"}]}"}}]},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"tool_calls"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":30033,"completion_tokens":1080,"total_tokens":31113,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":29824},"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":652},"prompt_cache_hit_tokens":29824,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":209},"system_fingerprint":"a26a7955944dc5c60445bff77fac9c8e"}
